text: Harbury team, this is Grace Wanjiru, the CHV from Rongai. I want to report on today's family planning outreach at Kampia Motor Dispensary. We started at 9 in the morning with a short talk on the different methods than the nurse, Sister Mary Chebet, gave services. In total, 42 women came, and most of them were young mothers. Six women were referred to Rongai Health Center for Implants because we ran out of stock. One mama asked to be called for follow-up, her number is 0711 000 482. I will send the register tomorrow. Thank you.

text: Hi team, The Beatrice Artino here, reporting from the Too Many Women's Group meeting in Mogosho. Today was our monthly table banking day. 25 members attended out of 30. Together they saved 18,000 shillings, and we gave out four small loans to members who are starting businesses, mostly selling vegetables and second-hand clothes. The treasurer, Mama Lucy Kiprop, recorded everything in the book. Our next meeting is on the 15th. If you need the records, Lucy's number is 0745 000 638.

text: Morning everyone, this is Janet Mwangi. Yesterday we went to Sarambia Primary School for the menstrual hygiene session with the girls in class 6 to 8. 60 girls attended. We talked about periods, how to use and dispose of pads safely, and why they should not miss school. At the end, every girl received a pack of reusable sanitary pads. The head teacher, Mrs. Esther Koch, has asked us to come back and also talk to the mothers. Her phone number is 0790 000 274 if someone wants to follow up.

text: Hello team, it's Masi Wambui. I want to share about the community dialogue on gender-based violence we held this afternoon at the chief's camp in Solai. 35 women attended, plus a few village elders. The police gender desk officer, Corporal and Mutua, explained how to report cases and where survivors can get help. Some women shared their stories, it was very emotional. Three women asked for private follow-up, and we connected them with the counselor. For anything about this session, you can call me on 0701 000 593.

text: Hello team, this is Caroline Nyambura reporting from Kampiamoto. Today we held the kitchen garden training for women farmers. 18 women attended. The agriculture officer, Mr. Peter Langart, showed them how to make a sack garden and how to make compost from kitchen waste. Each woman received seedlings of Tsukuma wiki and spinach to plant at home. Next month we will visit their homes to see how the gardens are doing. If you want to join the follow-up visits, call me on 0712 000 765.
